key_verdict: No disagreement; the setter's key is correct in all three parts.
fixes: (c) makes two demands (compute (1 -1)C AND interpret its element) for one mark; SEAB pays a matrix operation and its interpretation separately. Either give (c) [2] and let the slot carry 5 marks (take one from elsewhere in the paper), or keep [1] and ask only 'Explain what the element of the matrix (1 -1)C represents' so the arithmetic is implicit.

The stem introduces the labels rice (R), eggs (E) and cooking oil (O) but never uses them. Either drop the bracketed letters or print them as column headings above P (and rows A, B beside it), which is how a real paper would use them.
Minor register: '(a) Represent the numbers of items Mrs Tan needs to buy' reads better as 'Represent the number of each item Mrs Tan needs to buy in a 3 x 1 matrix Q.'
why: The rewritten skeleton is no longer the 2017 P1 Q19 shape: the given matrix is now a price table rather than usage counts, there is no unknown x inside a matrix, the candidate writes a single shopping-list column, and the closing move is a (1 -1) pre-multiplication read in context rather than 'the two totals are equal, find x'; numbers are exam-clean and the 4-mark weight fits the Q21 slot. It stops short of 5 only on mark discipline in (c) and the unused R/E/O labels.
